location: §6.2 "Olmo 3 RL-Zero can strongly improve on reasoning"
quote: We also see a decent improvement in pass@32 results, demonstrating that our run maintains diversity and RLVR pushes the model beyond its initial capabilities.
supports: The Olmo 3 report reads the 7B RL-Zero run's pass@32 gain as RL going beyond the base's initial capabilities.

quote: AIME 2024 and 2025 with pass@1, computed as a bootstrapped average over 32 samples, and pass@32.
supports: Olmo 3's RL-Zero evaluation uses 32 samples (pass@1 and pass@32) on AIME 2024/2025.

location: §4.5 "DPO and SFT both benefit from RL, but DPO remains a better starting point"
quote: while the DPO model does display lower entropy, it in fact has higher pass@K performance on AIME evaluations
supports: The Olmo 3 report finds the Think DPO model has higher AIME pass@K than the SFT model despite lower entropy.

location: §4.5 "DPO and SFT both benefit from RL, but DPO remains a better starting point"
quote: RLVR, under certain conditions, helps convert pass@K improvements into pass@1 gains.
supports: The Olmo 3 report frames RL from the DPO start as converting pass@K into pass@1, citing Yue et al.

quote: RL expands a model’s reasoning boundary most effectively in domains where the base model initially struggles.
supports: ProRL's headline: RL's boundary expansion is largest where the base is weakest.

quote: we observe a significant negative correlation between the base model’s reasoning boundary and the extent of reasoning improvement after RL training.
supports: ProRL reports a negative correlation between base pass@128 and the post-RL improvement (no coefficient in the sentence).

quote: For other tasks (logical puzzles and instruction following), we calculate the average continuous reward score from our rule-based verifiers.
supports: ProRL scores instruction following (and logic puzzles) by average continuous verifier reward, not binary pass.

quote: we increase inference samples to 256 and re-evaluate performance.
supports: ProRL's boundary analysis draws 256 samples per prompt.

quote: base models consistently surpass RLVR models across all benchmarks and LLM families as k increases.
supports: Yue et al. find base models overtake their RLVR models at large k on every benchmark and model family tested.

quote: with up to 5 constraints, which are sampled from IFEval (Zhou et al., 2023) and IFBench-Train (Pyatkin et al., 2025).
supports: Olmo 3 Think RL instruction-following prompts carry constraints sampled from IFEval and IFBench-Train.

quote: We audited all 2821 rewarded FPs in family A under written, human-adjudicated rules. Of these, 47.57% (record-weighted) are verified-wrong
supports: A human-adjudicated audit of every rewarded false positive in one code-RL family finds about half are genuinely wrong code.

quote: Manual inspection of model responses shows that, for most problems, the base model can produce at least one correct CoT
supports: Yue et al. find by manual inspection that the base produces at least one correct chain of thought on most problems.

quote: only one narrowly meets this criterion before multiplicity adjustment
supports: Of nine public RLVR checkpoints, only one narrowly meets the paper's certified-crossover criterion before multiplicity adjustment.
